clue.text: Ordinary people trio bored in Great Escape?

definitions.meaning: a stock phrase for just anybody, the common run of folk
in the film The Great Escape the prisoners dig three tunnels with these three code names

explanation.surface: A film buff wonders whether the common folk were bored watching The Great Escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' looks like 'uninterested' but means 'dug': the three tunnels in the 1963 prisoner-of-war film.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names three random men to mean anyone at all, the general public.

clue.text: Walked street with umbrella thus?

parts.note: a furled umbrella is carried rolled up, so this is how the umbrella is

explanation.surface: Someone went for a walk down the street with an umbrella, presumably furled.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll is to walk at a leisurely pace, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Depression controlled when one swallowed sedative

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land

indicators.note: the word for controlled takes in the numeral, as if swallowing it

parts.note: to run a business is to control it, so ran
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A pill was swallowed while someone was feeling low and under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerian root is a traditional herbal remedy taken as a mild sedative.

clue.text: International blog excited American learner

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the four letters of blog are jumbled

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: An American student gets worked up about an international blog.
explanation.definitionFit: Something international spans many nations, which is what worldwide or global means.

clue.text: Prisoner French marshal beheaded in river

indicators.note: the shortened marshal's name is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the Welsh border

indicators.note: the marshal's name loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: Philippe Pétain was a Marshal of France, later head of the Vichy regime

explanation.surface: A French marshal, now a prisoner, was beheaded in a river — a grim historical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a marshal executed by beheading; Pétain was in fact sentenced to death, then spared. Here 'beheaded' only drops his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is someone held in custody, which is a prisoner by another name.

clue.text: Radical Yankee in revolutionary éclat

indicators.note: the Y is placed inside the jumbled letters
revolutionary letters are overturned and rearranged, so éclat is jumbled

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A radical American makes a splash with revolutionary flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ECLAT into ACETL, and 'in' puts Y inside it. 'Radical' looks political, but in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetyl is a chemical group (CH3CO) that behaves as one unit in compounds, which chemists call a radical.

clue.text: Noted miniatures unfortunately in deficient appraisal

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A collector's notable miniatures were sadly given too low a valuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Underestimation is valuing something too low, an appraisal that falls short.

clue.text: Informed about article with book complete

parts.note: on means concerning, as in a talk on art
the is the definite article
all means whole or complete

explanation.surface: Someone well read about a newspaper article and a whole book.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball means being alert and up to date, so well informed.

clue.text: Spy on box always one to catch as plot developed

indicators.note: the word for always plus the numeral catch the jumbled letters inside them

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: a developed plot has its letters worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A TV spy story: always someone to catch as the plot unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' turns AS PLOT into POLAST, which 'to catch' puts inside EVERI. 'Box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: The MI5 officer played by Sandra Oh in the BBC series Killing Eve is a television spy.

clue.text: One now liberated as political defector?

definitions.meaning: a former convict, released from prison
someone who has left the Conservative Party, a former Con

explanation.surface: A defector who has now been freed from a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is short for Conservative in British politics as well as for convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A released prisoner is a former convict; a Tory who quits is a former Conservative.

clue.text: See woman commander taking bearings

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
OC stands for Officer Commanding
ESE, east-south-east, combines compass bearings

explanation.surface: A female commander takes her bearings and looks around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the noun, a bishop's seat, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district under that bishop's authority, the same as a diocese.

clue.text: Busy worker round wine town finds little animal

indicators.note: the insect goes round the town's name

parts.note: the bee is proverbially busy and a worker bee does the hive's labour
Asti is a town in Piedmont famous for its sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A hard worker touring an Italian wine town comes across a small creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastie is a Scots diminutive for any small creature, as in Burns's poem To a Mouse.

clue.text: One made to shoot young horse

definitions.meaning: a firearm, specifically the ... revolver made by Samuel ... company

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a famous make of revolver and a male foal under four years old.

clue.text: Very sick girl in A&E one obsessed with 9 18

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: the girl's name goes inside the two letters

parts.note: the letters A and E, from accident and emergency, a British hospital casualty unit
Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A very sick girl lies in hospital casualty, fixated on a TV spy.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: In Killing Eve the assassin is fixated on the MI5 agent who hunts her.

clue.text: Incredibly bad sign for corporation

indicators.note: incredibly suggests something unbelievable, signalling that the letters of bad are reworked

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: An unbelievably bad portent for a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a business but is old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is jocular dated slang for a large belly, that is the stomach region.

clue.text: Dark treacle in short while found by girls

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short while
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Some girls find dark treacle in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the dark syrup left from refining sugar, much like black treacle.

clue.text: Shabby theatre bound to appear in correspondence

indicators.note: the word for bound shows up inside the word for correspondence

parts.note: a fit is a match or correspondence between two things
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A run-down theatre is obliged to feature in the letters page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'obliged' and 'correspondence' like letters; one is a jump, the other a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleapit is British slang for a scruffy old cinema or theatre, supposedly flea-ridden.

clue.text: Cope with assassin — here's light cannon

parts.note: to field a question is to deal with or cope with it
a gun is a hired killer, a gunman

explanation.surface: Someone must handle a hitman, and here is a small cannon to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: A field gun is a light artillery piece built to move with troops.

clue.text: See 9
Female in hat after protest broke down

indicators.note: the hat piece comes after the protest

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: the pronoun goes inside the word for hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman in a hat broke down after a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish is to knock down a building, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Penning one is each MP's need originally

definitions.text: Penning one is each MP's need originally

parts.words: Penning one is each MP's need originally
parts.note: every newly elected member of parliament must write and deliver a first address to the House

explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' signals the first one, not first letters of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A new MP's first address to the Commons is traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: See 20
Severely criticise Casablancan pianist drinking litre?

indicators.note: the pianist takes the abbreviation inside, as if drinking it

parts.note: Sam is the pianist in the film Casablanca, told to play As Time Goes By

explanation.surface: Was the pianist in Casablanca drinking by the litre?
explanation.definitionFit: To slam a play or book is to criticise it harshly.

clue.text: First-rate paper under discussion

parts.note: A is the top grade, so first-rate
tissue is a thin soft paper

explanation.surface: A top-quality paper is being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: A point at issue is one being debated, in dispute.

clue.text: Security is brought back into store

indicators.note: the turned letters go into the word for store

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: the two letters of is are brought back, read in the other direction

explanation.surface: A security guard is brought back into the store.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is money held as security against loss or damage.

clue.text: Trump shot perhaps? Urn needed

definitions.meaning: Judd Trump is a snooker champion, and sinking a ball in snooker is this kind of shot
an urn is a vessel or jar

explanation.surface: Has the President taken a shot? An urn is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' suggests the politician or a card game, but it is snooker's Judd Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a successful shot sinks the ball, and the same word means a container like an urn.

clue.text: Woman tempted after scripture class — that's official

indicators.note: the woman's name follows the class

parts.note: RE is religious education, school scripture lessons
Eve was tempted by the serpent in Eden

explanation.surface: A woman is tempted after religious class, and that's official.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval local officer, such as a shire reeve or sheriff.

clue.text: Against noble visiting monarch, summit curtailed

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: the word for summit loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: the top is the summit

explanation.surface: A nobleman opposed to the king visits, his summit cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Counter to means contrary to or in opposition to, so against.
